parameters.identity: Source: a small rigid rectangular cream cheese package with a pale gray-blue planar top, large outlined 'Cream Cheese' script, and a narrow dark-blue oval emblem. Its right and near side faces are visible, and it lies flat on the exposed wooden tabletop. Destination: the open round bowl with dense black-and-white interior patterning, a thin yellowish rim, and dark exterior. The bowl is empty and distinct from the nearby white plate with red rings. No grasp or retention is present in these images.
landmark_definitions: l0: The initial capital C in the large printed word 'Cream', at the center of its curved stroke.
l1: The terminal curled stroke of the final letter in the large printed word 'Cheese'.
l2: The midpoint of the long outer border of the dark-blue oval emblem, on the side opposite the large Cream Cheese script.

evidence.explanation: The source is the rigid rectangular cream cheese package lying label-up on the tabletop beside the bowl. Its planar printed top and narrow visible side faces support a flat resting pose on that single support; its underside is not visible or inferred from a top sample. The destination is the empty, open, approximately circular patterned bowl, not the striped plate. Its inner rim and cavity bottom are visible, with no observed obstruction across the opening. All measurements below are from the current wrist image. The textured patch is inside the source package's printed top face. These observations establish local object eligibility, not clearance for an entire transfer.

evidence.explanation: The proposed high_alignment action is locally supported with the gripper open. Current and earlier images show the same cream cheese package, printed landmarks, bowl and support surfaces, with no observed displacement or intervening interaction. This is a nearly level translation above the package, not a descent or grasp. The supplied own-finger envelope has its lowest extent near 1.174 m, well above the observed package top near 0.918 m, bowl lip near 0.948 m and tabletop near 0.900 m. The visible bottle and fixtures do not present external material obstructing this high alignment. The end-biased target is not inconsistent with the package identity or geometry. Some immediate hand surroundings are hidden by the robot itself; this is self-occlusion, not an external obstacle. No upward observation action is needed to justify this alignment. Returned landmarks and surface regions provide current measurements rather than relying on saved points. This finding does not approve a later descent, certify a complete corridor, establish retention, or indicate task completion.

The proposed open-hand descent to the source_hover pad target is locally supported, only to that hover height. The current package outline, Cream Cheese lettering and emblem agree with the earlier identity and stationary landmark projections. The fixed agentview also shows no source or bowl displacement. The acknowledged high, open-hand approach shows no evidence of disturbing interaction, so the saved source, bowl and support geometry remains a usable short-horizon prior here.

The visible tabletop flanks both actual finger lanes near the selected package end. The bowl is offset from those lanes; no external material is observed obstructing this descent. Using the supplied final finger envelope, its lowest height is approximately 0.9546 m, about 0.036 m above the package top and 0.0069 m above the saved rim height. The nearby bowl material is also horizontally separated from the end-biased finger footprint. The approximately 0.0135 m longitudinal pad/side overlap is finite despite the end bias, but this hover stops above side contact and does not establish a grasp.

Current measurements are returned below, including bowl and support observations. The wrist-view projection of k2 is covered by the robot, so k2 is selected in agentview instead. That self-occlusion does not hide the relevant descent lanes in the combined views. Bowl region bounds include surrounding background for boundary fitting. This finding is not certified clearance, retention evidence, or approval of a subsequent contact descent, closing action or transfer.

The proposed open-hand grasp descent is locally supported. The current package outline, visible end face and printed landmarks agree with the earlier stationary cream cheese package; no target displacement or inconsistent identity is observed. The preceding approach remains consistent with noncontact motion. Visible bowl portions also agree with the earlier pose.

Both actual lateral finger lanes project onto exposed tabletop, outside the package sides. The supplied own geometry and observed package end support an end-biased pinch: approximately 13 mm of longitudinal pad/side overlap remains, with finite vertical overlap at the proposed pad height. Centering on the package length is not necessary. The proposed endpoint has only about 3 mm nominal lowest-finger clearance above the observed table, so this assessment supports the specified endpoint and orientation, not a deeper descent. No external material is observed obstructing these lanes; the nearby bowl is separated from this end of the package. This is not certified clearance or support for a later transport corridor.

Self-occlusion hides the far package corner insets, bowl landmarks k4 and k5, and stove_burner_top; those measurements cannot be freshly returned. Other obtainable historical named points are returned below using current visible surfaces. The visible partial source and bowl observations support retaining their stationary geometry only for this short local action. No grasp, retention, placement or task completion is claimed.

Bracketing is observed in frame 114. The actual open fingers are visible on opposite sides of the cream cheese package. Agentview shows both lowered finger tips beside the exposed package end; the wrist view independently shows both fingers and visible tabletop gaps separating them from the package. Compared with the earlier images, the fingers have descended alongside this same item. No table penetration or neighboring-object intrusion is observed in this local bracketing area. The gripper housing self-occludes the rest of the package and portions of the inner finger surfaces; those hidden surfaces are not certified. This is a pre-closure observation, not evidence of retention or task completion.
